title: Armored Core: Project Phantasma
subtitle: An earlier contract in the same world

body: Armored Core: Project Phantasma is FromSoftware's second PlayStation mecha action game, first released in Japan on 4 December 1997. Set before the original Armored Core, it sends the mercenary pilot to investigate the Amber Crown complex and the research conducted there by the Doomsday Organization. An escaped prisoner, Sumika, becomes an ally while the rival pilot Stinger pursues them. The campaign gives this return to the workshop and battlefield a more concentrated storyline, keeping the first game's connection between paid missions, equipment and the machine assembled by the player.

Save data from Armored Core can be imported, carrying a developed pilot and equipment into the new game. Additional weapons and parts expand the choices available in the garage. The underlying combat remains familiar, so a returning player can use knowledge of movement and equipment while responding to new missions. That continuity makes the sequel feel like another assignment within an established career. A build that worked before remains a starting point, but the player still has to decide whether its strengths suit the situation now being presented.

The new Arena mode gives the player another use for a customised Armored Core: a direct confrontation with another pilot. Away from a mission's changing objectives, the encounter concentrates attention on how two machines move and fight. It became a foundation for the next release, Master of Arena, where competitive rankings would take a larger role. Project Phantasma reached North America in 1998 but was not released in Europe. Within the original trilogy it supplies both a narrative prequel and an important addition to the series' structure of mercenary work.
